interest: This file provides a valuable window into Japanese economic diplomacy, covert procurement efforts, and intelligence concerns in the Caribbean on the eve of World War II. It illustrates how Japanese commercial networks—notably the Mitsui Company and the Exporters' Federation of Japan—sought alternative sources for vital war-related raw materials like salt for caustic soda and attempted sanctions evasion by recruiting an American mechanic to smuggle aviation engine parts. Additionally, FBI communications and State Department surveillance demonstrate inter-agency intelligence coordination regarding Latin American loyalties, pre-Pearl Harbor evacuations of Japanese nationals, and wartime internment policies in the Dominican Republic.
overview: This file (894.20239) covers Japanese commercial, espionage, and political activities in the Dominican Republic between April 1940 and January 1942, spanning the immediate run-up to and aftermath of the United States' entry into World War II. The collection consists of State Department cross-reference sheets, an original two-page diplomatic despatch from the U.S. Legation in Ciudad Trujillo, and a confidential memorandum from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover. Key subjects include promotional trade tours by Japanese trade representatives, an illicit attempt to recruit an American mechanic in the Dominican Air Corps to re-export aviation engines to Japan, large-scale Japanese purchases of pure rock salt from Barahona mines by the Mitsui Company to replace disrupted East African supplies, alleged political interference involving Esteban Prieto and Elie Lescot, the evacuation of Japanese nationals in mid-November 1941, and the wartime internment of the last remaining Japanese resident in early 1942.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a quarterly report on visits to the Dominican Republic by the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires in Havana and trade federation president Saburo Nango.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 1190 of April 5, 1940, from the U.S. Legation in the Dominican Republic. It notes a quarterly report detailing a quiet February visit by the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires stationed in Havana, followed by a highly publicized visit on March 29 by Saburo Nango, President of the Exporters' Federation of Japan. The despatch also highlighted Nango's statements to the local press regarding opportunities for commercial interchange between Japan and the Dominican Republic.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 1190 on Japanese activities and visit of Saburo Nango

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording an attempt by a Japanese agent to smuggle aviation engines and parts out of the Dominican Republic to Japan.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 1270 of June 15, 1940, from the U.S. Legation in the Dominican Republic. It reports an effort by Kiyoshi Mitzutani, a local representative of the Exporters' Federation of Japan, to induce American aircraft mechanic George Burrie of the Dominican Air Corps to import aviation motors and components into the Dominican Republic for covert re-export to Japan aboard ships of the N.Y.K. Line. The original paper was filed under 800.20210/544.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 1270 on attempted procurement of aviation motors

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 154 regarding the purity of Dominican salt exports and purchase intentions of the Mitsui Company.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 154 dated October 15, 1940, from the U.S. Legation in the Dominican Republic. It addresses allegations by C. R. Thomas that salt shipped to Japan from government mines was tainted with gypsum, correcting the record to note that the salt was 99% pure. It also states that the Mitsui Company planned to make further purchases unless Japan became involved in a war.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 154 on purchase of Dominican salt by Japan

subfiles.about: Despatch from the U.S. Legation in Ciudad Trujillo refuting claims of gypsum contamination in Dominican rock salt purchased by Japan for caustic soda manufacturing.
subfiles.from: Robert M. Scotten (U.S. Legation, Ciudad Trujillo)
subfiles.summary: U.S. Minister Robert M. Scotten replies to the State Department's confidential instruction regarding a report from C. R. Thomas that salt exported to Japan from government mines at Barahona was contaminated with gypsum. Scotten explains that inquiries revealed the salt is over 99% pure, with gypsum existing in separate deposits, and that Japan purchased the mineral primarily to produce caustic soda. He notes that a visiting Mitsui Company representative anticipated continued purchases barring war, and concludes that the transaction was a legitimate commercial substitution for Ethiopian supplies cut off via Djibouti.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 154 from Ciudad Trujillo on purchase by Japan of Dominican salt

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 361 concerning alleged Japanese subversive activities and interference in Dominican domestic politics.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet references Despatch No. 361 of April 16, 1941, sent by U.S. Minister Robert M. Scotten from the Dominican Republic. It indexes reporting on alleged Japanese subversive activities and an attempted intervention in Dominican domestic politics. The underlying original paper was catalogued under file number 894.20238/4.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 361 on alleged Japanese subversive activities

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a report on proposals made by Esteban Prieto to Elie Lescot regarding Japanese political interference in the Dominican Republic.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet references Despatch No. 361 dated April 16, 1941, originating from the U.S. Legation in the Dominican Republic. It indexes a report concerning political overtures and proposals made by Esteban Prieto to Haitian diplomat Elie Lescot regarding a suspected Japanese scheme to meddle in Dominican politics. The original document was preserved under file number 894.20210 Prieto, Esteban/7.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 361 on proposals by Esteban Prieto to Elie Lescot

subfiles.about: Confidential letter from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover reporting the departure of Japanese nationals from the Dominican Republic in November 1941.
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover (Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation)
subfiles.summary: FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover writes a personal and confidential letter by special message to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr., copied to Naval Intelligence and Army G-2. Hoover reports confidential intelligence that Japanese nationals residing in the Dominican Republic departed the country around mid-November 1941, just weeks prior to the attack on Pearl Harbor. The communication also notes that strong pro-United States sentiment prevailed throughout the Dominican Republic.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. regarding departure of Japanese nationals
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (Assistant Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram reporting an absence of Japanese propaganda and the internment of the only remaining Japanese resident.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram No. 4 (sent at 10:00 a.m. on January 7, 1942) from U.S. Minister Robert M. Scotten in Ciudad Trujillo. It records that there was no evidence of Japanese propaganda operations within the Dominican Republic following the outbreak of the Pacific War. Scotten also noted that the single Japanese resident remaining in the country was held in a concentration camp.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 4 on Japanese propaganda and internment
